value.rationale: The sharp norm on the canonical three-dimensional Bergman polynomial subspace is a natural finite-degree counterpart to contractive inequalities. The theorem resolves a nontrivial qualitative optimizer-support question at every weight and obtains the sharp first nonzero correction to the monomial lower bound as the radial weight concentrates, quantifying mode mixing not inferred from classical dilation bounds. It does not require a finite-beta closed form or full general-degree embedding theorem to be mathematically substantive.
